questions.q: What does Goal Seek fundamentally do differently from how a formula normally works?
options: It solves backward — you supply the target result, and it finds the input value that produces it
It only formats cells, without changing any values
It runs a formula forward faster than normal
It automatically creates a chart from your formula's results
questions.explain: Normally you plug in inputs and read the result. Goal Seek reverses that: you already know the target result, and it searches for the input value that gets a formula to land on it.

questions.q: In the Goal Seek dialog, what must the 'Set cell' contain?
options: The formula whose result you're targeting — never a plain input value
The exact target number itself
The input cell that will be adjusted
A chart of the results
questions.explain: Set cell must hold the formula whose output you care about. The target number goes in 'To value', and the input Goal Seek adjusts goes in 'By changing cell'.

questions.q: In the worked example — Unit Price × Units Sold = Total Revenue, targeting $50,000 — which field would 'Unit Price' go into?
options: By changing cell
Set cell
To value
None of the three fields — Unit Price isn't used
questions.explain: Unit Price is the input being solved for, so it belongs in 'By changing cell'. The Total Revenue formula cell is the Set cell, and 50000 is the To value.

questions.q: How many input cells can a single Goal Seek run adjust?
options: Exactly one — the cell named in 'By changing cell'
As many as you like, all at once
Zero — Goal Seek only reads values, never changes them
It depends on how many cells the formula references
questions.explain: Goal Seek adjusts exactly one input cell per run to try to hit the target — for scenarios with multiple simultaneous unknowns, Goal Seek isn't the right tool.

questions.q: How does a Data Table differ from Goal Seek, per this lesson's one-sentence contrast?
options: A Data Table tests many different input scenarios at once, rather than solving backward for a single target the way Goal Seek does
A Data Table and Goal Seek are identical features with different names
A Data Table only works with text data, never numbers
A Data Table replaces the need for formulas entirely
questions.explain: Goal Seek solves for one target using one changing input. A Data Table instead shows results across a whole range of input values side by side — a different job, both under the What-If Analysis menu.
